source_refs.note: Exercise 2.7, Question 4 (book page 70). The book prints no answers for Unit 2; results verified with sympy.

blocks.prompt: 4. A wire of 20 meters is cut into two pieces. One piece is bent into a square and the other into a circle. How should the wire be cut to maximize the total area enclosed?
blocks.explanation:
A maximum problem on a closed interval: the cut can be anywhere from 0 to 20 m.
Given: 20 m of wire, one piece makes a square, the other a circle. To find: where to cut for the largest total area.
Plan: form \(A(x)\), find the critical point, test it; if it is a minimum, compare the end points \(x = 0\) and \(x = 20\).
steps:
Given: wire 20 m; piece \(x\) m bent into a square, the rest \((20 - x)\) m into a circle, \(0 \le x \le 20\).
To find: the cut that makes the total area greatest.
Method: total area as a function of \(x\); critical point and second derivative test; on a closed interval also check the end points.

Area of each shape
Square: perimeter \(4a = x\), so \(a = \frac{x}{4}\), area \(\frac{x^{2}}{16}\).
Circle: \(2\pi R = 20 - x\), so \(R = \frac{20 - x}{2\pi}\), area \(\pi R^{2} = \frac{(20 - x)^{2}}{4\pi}\).
\[A(x) = \dfrac{x^{2}}{16} + \dfrac{(20 - x)^{2}}{4\pi} \quad \text{...(1)}\]
Why: the wire becomes the boundary of each shape.

Critical point
\[\dfrac{dA}{dx} = \dfrac{x}{8} - \dfrac{20 - x}{2\pi} \quad \text{...(2)}\]
\[\pi x - 4(20 - x) = 0 \Rightarrow (4 + \pi)x = 80\]
\[x = \dfrac{80}{4 + \pi} \approx 11.20\text{ m}\]
Why: chain rule on \((20 - x)^{2}\) gives \(2(20 - x)(-1)\); multiply the equation by \(8\pi\).

Second derivative test
\[\dfrac{d^{2}A}{dx^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{8} + \dfrac{1}{2\pi} > 0\]
Why: positive, so this critical point gives the minimum total area, not the maximum. There \(A_{\min} = \frac{100}{4 + \pi} \approx 14.00\text{ m}^{2}\).

Compare the end points
\[x = 0: \ A(0) = \dfrac{400}{4\pi} = \dfrac{100}{\pi} \approx 31.83\text{ m}^{2}\]
\[x = 20: \ A(20) = \dfrac{400}{16} = 25\text{ m}^{2}\]
Why: a continuous function on a closed interval takes its greatest value at a critical point or at an end point. The only critical point is a minimum, so the maximum is at an end point (see the graph).

Interpret
The greatest area, \(\frac{100}{\pi} \approx 31.83\text{ m}^{2}\), comes when all the wire is bent into the circle (\(x = 0\)).
Why: a circle encloses more area than a square of the same perimeter. If the wire must really be cut into two pieces, the square piece should be as short as possible.

Check
\[A(0) = 31.83 > A(20) = 25 > A\!\left(\tfrac{80}{4 + \pi}\right) \approx 14.00\]
At \(x = \frac{80}{4 + \pi}\): square side \(\frac{20}{4 + \pi}\), circle radius \(\frac{10}{4 + \pi}\), and \(\frac{400 + 100\pi}{(4 + \pi)^{2}} = \frac{100}{4 + \pi}\) ✓.
blocks.final_answer: Maximum: use the whole 20 m (or as much as possible) for the circle; the greatest area is \(\frac{100}{\pi} \approx 31.83\text{ m}^{2}\). (Cutting at \(\frac{80}{4 + \pi} \approx 11.20\) m for the square and \(\frac{20\pi}{4 + \pi} \approx 8.80\) m for the circle gives the minimum area \(\frac{100}{4 + \pi} \approx 14.00\text{ m}^{2}\).)

answer_figure.alt: Graph of the total area A(x) = x squared over 16 plus (20 minus x) squared over 4 pi for x from 0 to 20. The curve falls from (0, 31.83) to its lowest point (11.20, 14.00) and rises to (20, 25). The highest value is at x = 0, all wire in the circle.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The question asks for the cut that maximizes the total area, but the only critical point, \(x = \frac{80}{4 + \pi}\), gives the minimum area (\(\frac{d^{2}A}{dx^{2}} > 0\)). The maximum is at the end point \(x = 0\): no square at all, the whole wire bent into a circle, area \(\frac{100}{\pi} \approx 31.83\text{ m}^{2}\). If the book intended "minimize the total area", the answer is: square piece \(\frac{80}{4 + \pi} \approx 11.20\) m, circle piece \(\frac{20\pi}{4 + \pi} \approx 8.80\) m, least area \(\frac{100}{4 + \pi} \approx 14.00\text{ m}^{2}\).
